title: ’’I didn’t think a podium would come this early’’: Yevan - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 5 (Daily Mirror) - "It's a pretty crazy feeling, honestly. Walking into the F1 paddock now... it's just an incredible feeling," said Yevan David after making history with a sensational second-place finish in the FIA Formula 3 Sprint Race at the iconic Silverstone Circuit.

Driving for AIX Racing, David delivered a composed and determined performance to secure his maiden FIA Formula 3 podium, becoming the first Sri Lankan driver to finish on the podium in the championship.

Starting from the front row of the grid, David maintained a strong pace throughout the race and successfully defended his position under relentless pressure from the chasing pack during the closing laps. Despite the race winner pulling away at the front, the Sri Lankan youngster remained calm and consistent to cross the finish line in second place.

"I didn't think a podium would come this early," he said, adding that he was "very proud" of both himself and Sri Lanka.

title: Update: Two prisoners killed, over 25 injured in Negombo Prison violence - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 5 (Daily Mirror) - Two inmates were killed and more than 25 others injured following a clash between two groups of prisoners at the Negombo Prison on Saturday, hospital sources said.

The clash reportedly broke out around noon inside the prison. The circumstances leading to the incident have not yet been disclosed.

More than 25 injured inmates were admitted to the Negombo Hospital for treatment. Hospital sources confirmed that two of the injured prisoners later succumbed to their injuries.

title: 8 shot, including 4 children, in Coney Island, NYPD says - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
abc NEWS - At least eight people, including four children, were shot during an incident in Brooklyn's Coney Island late on the Fourth of July, the New York Police Department said.

Officers responded at about 10:37 p.m. to reports of a shooting on the 2900 block of West 31st Street, the NYPD said in a statement.

The injured, who were not publicly identified, included a 37-year-old man, a 33-year-old man, a 25-year-old woman, a 21-year-old woman, a 14-year-old boy, a 12-year-old boy, a 7-year-old boy and a 6-year-old boy.

"All victims were transported by EMS to local area hospitals where seven people were listed in stable condition," the NYPD said. "The 21-year-old woman is listed in critical condition."

Police said they recovered a firearm at the scene but have not made any arrests.

title: 75 drowning fatalities recorded so far this year - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 5 (Daily Mirror) - At least 75 people have lost their lives in drowning incidents during the first months of this year.

According to Police, the majority of the fatal incidents occurred when individuals entered unmonitored or hazardous locations to bathe or swim.

Police statistics also show that drowning remains a significant public safety concern, with 450 drowning-related deaths recorded across the country in 2025.

In view of the continuing fatalities, the Police has urged the public and tourists to avoid entering water at locations identified as unsafe and to exercise extreme caution when visiting rivers, reservoirs, beaches and other water bodies.

title: Missing service weapon of Yatiyantota Traffic OIC recovered from Kelani River - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 5 (Daily Mirror) - The official service firearm belonging to the Officer-in-Charge (OIC) of the Traffic Branch of the Yatiyantota Police, which had been reported missing, has been recovered from the Kelani River.

According to the police, a stock of ammunition was also retrieved from the river along with the weapon.

The Traffic OIC was arrested on June 28 on charges of failing to properly hand over his official service firearm and 10 rounds of ammunition. Following his arrest, he was produced before the Ruwanwella Magistrate's Court and subsequently remanded in custody.

title: Mexico return luxury watches gifted by YouTuber - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
BBC - The American YouTuber, whose real name is Stephen Deleonardis, says he spent $1m (£747,000) on Rolex watches for every Mexico player and member of staff.

The World Cup co-hosts play England at Mexico City's Azteca Stadium on Sunday evening local time (01:00 BST, Monday).

Deleonardis presented them to the squad, external when he met them on Monday, the day before the World Cup co-hosts beat Ecuador in the last 32.

However, Fifa's Code of Ethics, external has restrictions on offering and accepting gifts, with article 21 stating that such gifts can only be offered or accepted if they "have symbolic or trivial value".

According to a post on the team's X account, external the Mexico players decided to return the watches "by mutual agreement" and that Stevewilldoit had gifted them "on his own initiative".

They are hoping to reach the quarter-finals for the first time since hosting the World Cup in 1986.

title: Government committed to equipping children with modern skills: PM - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 5 (Daily Mirror) - Prime Minister Harini Amarasuriya said the Government is committed to equipping Sri Lankan children with the knowledge, skills and modern technologies needed to realise their full potential, while fostering creativity and critical thinking through education reforms.

The Prime Minister made these remarks while attending the opening of the 'Arumasiya' exhibition and the foundation stone-laying ceremony for a new three-storey building at Balangoda Vidyaloka Central College on Friday (July 4).

During the visit, Dr. Amarasuriya officially declared open the exhibition, which showcased students' innovations and creative talents, and praised them for demonstrating skills that extend beyond textbook learning.

Addressing the gathering, she said the Government is introducing a new education reform programme aimed at replacing the traditional examination-oriented system with a more practical and skills-based approach. She noted that preparations are currently underway to implement the reforms from 2027.

The Prime Minister said the objective is to ensure that every student leaving school has access to vocational and technical education suited to their talents and aligned with the needs of the modern labour market. She added that the Government is also working to elevate vocational education to enjoy the same recognition and dignity as university education.

Dr. Amarasuriya also commended the principal, academic staff, students and parents of Balangoda Vidyaloka Central College for organising the exhibition and contributing to its success.

According to the Prime Minister's Media Division, the event was attended by Ratnapura District MPs Wasantha Pushpa Kumara and Sunil Rajapaksha, the Mayor of Balangoda, members of the Municipal Council, the Zonal Director of Education, the school's principal and academic staff, parents and students.
